messages:
Eli R.: Heads-up: design review for the Revoke Key flow. I pushed a new prototype that toggles between inline revoke + undo toast vs modal-confirm. Need opinions on friction, copy, and keyboard accessibility.

Priya K.: Saw it. Link: https://figma.com/file/efgh5678/revoke-flow-proto. My quick take: inline revoke with an undo toast feels less disruptive for short-lived mistakes, but we need a clear primary action and a way to escalate for org-admins who want stricter controls.

Tom S.: From an engineering/metrics POV, undo toast is easier (no extra roundtrip) and reduces abandonment. But we must be careful: revokes are security-sensitive. If user accidentally revokes a production key, an undo toast + 10s window might be insufficient. We should consider role-based behavior: admins see modal, others see toast.

Ava (a11y): Accessibility notes before we pick a pattern: 1) If toast-only, it must be accessible to screen reader users (announce toast as assertive and include action link "Undo"). 2) For modal option, ensure focus trap, focus on the modal heading, and ESC closes. 3) If we require typing a confirmation phrase (e.g., TYPE DELETE), ensure the input has clear label and aria-required.

Eli R.: Proposal: default to inline revoke + undo toast for keys marked non-production (scoped/ephemeral). For keys flagged as 'production' (manually tagged or by usage), require modal confirm with either a checkbox + reason field or a typed confirmation.

Priya K.: Copy ideas for inline toast: "Key revoked. Undo?" Maybe: "Key revoked — undo within 15s." For modal copy: "Revoke API key" heading, danger blurb: "Revoking will immediately invalidate the key and may break dependent services. This action cannot be undone without creating a new key."

Tom S.: If we do a 15s undo, backend needs to keep a soft-revoke state for that window. Not too hard but has design implications. Also we should emit an audit log entry at initial revoke time and another if undone.

Ava (a11y): Also: ensure undo action is reachable via keyboard (Tab to toast action) and has aria-label like "Undo revoke for key <key-name>". For the modal, add aria-describedby linking to the long explanation and include role="dialog" with aria-modal=true.

Eli R.: UX microcopy variants for modal confirm CTA: "Revoke key now" (danger) + secondary "Cancel". For typed confirm: placeholder text "Type REVOKE to confirm". Should the typed confirm be required only for production keys?

Priya K.: Yes, typed confirm for production keys only. For typed confirm copy, prefer the verb (REVOKE) over DELETE to match our product language.

Tom S.: One more thought: provide a keyboard shortcut to open the revoke modal when focused on a key row (e.g., press R). Might conflict. Probably better to avoid global shortcuts for destructive actions unless user explicitly triggers via menu.

Ava (a11y): Agree avoid single-key shortcuts for destructive actions. If we add a context menu -> Revoke, ensure menu items are keyboard navigable and include aria-keyshortcuts if we expose any complex combos.

Eli R.: Empty state after revoke: should we show an inline CTA to create a scoped key? Current mock shows a full-width card with illustration and two CTAs: "Create scoped key" and "Learn more about key best practices". Thoughts?

Priya K.: Keep it minimal: primary CTA "Create key" and a subtle link "Key best practices". For keyboard users, place primary as first focusable element. Also add quick bullets: scoped, ephemeral, rotate regularly.

Tom S.: Also add telemetry note: track which CTA is used from empty state to inform education.

Ava (a11y): Empty state must not rely on color alone. If we show an illustration, ensure alt text and provide visible focus outline on CTA. If we include a short checklist, use semantic list markup in the HTML so screen readers can parse it.

Eli R.: Next steps / action items: Priya to finalize copy for both toast and modal; Tom to confirm backend soft-revoke feasibility and audit logging; Ava to run a quick SR/VO test on both patterns; I'll update figma with admin vs non-admin branches and add examples of the typed confirm. Back in 24hrs for final decision. :thumbsup:

DevBot: Reminder: security review required for modal copy referencing "production" when rolled out beyond Beta.

Tom S.: I'll ping Security if we go with typed confirm for >0.5% of keys being production-class.

Eli R.: Thanks all — keeping this one small.
